meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. People draft somewhere else and paste it in. And you still haven't said whether Owen was heard first.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever happens next, none of this goes on his record, and none of it happens in front of his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misattribute quotations all the time, Hale. That's a citation error, not a crime.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then say what you intend to do about it, and tell me where his record stands right now.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. And you skipped my question: his record.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. He'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him, and nothing more. I want that email tonight, with his record and his class both in it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put the date in your email and he'll answer it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that commitment in writing, stating plainly that nothing is on his record now or will be, along with the proposed date so Owen can confirm it. I expect that email from you tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 and still wants your written commitment tonight that nothing goes on his record and nothing happens in front of his class, plus Owen's answer on the Thursday date; that is the fair outcome, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its dated times and then answering her paste-it-in defence by inviting a dated draft, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own document, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, even though she asked twice, so her procedural grievance stayed open the whole meeting.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, answer that plainly in one sentence before you turn the laptop around.
